title: Castle labelling sheet, six labels
subject: History
unit: Spring 2: Castles and Isambard Kingdom Brunel (Towers, Tunnels & Turrets)
source: Written for history/y2 lesson 6 (Castle labelling sheet, six labels (portal printable; assessed))
intro: Lesson 6: Parts of a castle. Listen, look, then do the tasks with a grown-up.

panels.title: Outside
points: Drawbridge: pulled up when danger came

parts.text: Find the water round the castle

keywords.def: the strongest tower, in the middle
a ditch of water round a castle
a bridge that can be pulled up
a heavy gate that drops down
the top of a wall with gaps

questions.q: What is the water round a castle called?
What could be pulled up when enemies came?
Where were guards to look out?
Core: Label six parts on the castle picture: keep, moat, drawbridge, portcullis, turret, battlements.
Extend: Write how the moat kept people safe.
questions.a: For example: enemies could not walk up to the walls

questions.q: Stretch: Which part would you add to make it safer?
A heavy gate that drops down is a:
questions.a: B) Portcullis. A portcullis drops down to block the gate. A moat is water; a turret is a small tower.

questions.q: The strongest tower in the middle is the:
Big question: which part would be hardest to get past?
questions.a: Any part with a reason, for example the moat, because you have to swim
